title: Kailasa temple: 2 lakh tonnes of rock, cut by hand, roof first
caption:
Kailasa temple, Ellora: India Built This #1. About 2 lakh tonnes of rock cut away by hand to leave one temple behind.

It was carved around 760 CE, under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, from the roof down: the sculptors worked top to bottom, so one wrong cut could not be fixed.

Extra: the courtyard around it is about 82 m by 46 m, and the rock block they freed is about 33 m high.

Nobody knows how long it took. One scholar's estimate is about 5.5 years with 250 workers; others say over a century. 5 years or 150? Comment your guess.

Every Thursday, one thing India built. Follow for #2.
